scoringMethod: scenario answer-key concept-strength matching with word-boundary, negation-aware terminology; grounding safety evaluated separately

modelResponse.episodeSummary: A 68-year-old male experienced sudden loss of consciousness during monitoring, preceded by crescendo chest pain and ST elevation. The event progressed to ventricular fibrillation (VF) cardiac arrest, requiring BLS/ACLS. The patient has a history of coronary artery disease and prior anterior MI.
modelResponse.mostLikelyEtiologyAndClinicalContext: Acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is the most likely etiology. This is supported by the patient's history of coronary artery disease, the preceding crescendo chest pain, ST elevation in V2-V4 on the 12-lead ECG 8 minutes prior to arrest, and markedly elevated cardiac biomarkers (troponin T 1.85 ng/mL, CK-MB 48 ng/mL). The STEMI likely led to myocardial ischemia, electrical instability (runs of PVCs, R-on-T phenomenon), and subsequent degeneration into ventricular fibrillation.
